rule: On a single-colour background with isolated 1s and 6s, every pair of 1s sharing a diagonal (same r-c or r+c) is joined by a diagonal segment of 1s painted on background cells. Every 6 strictly inside such a segment emits a full diagonal line of 6, perpendicular to the segment, out to both borders, again painting only background cells.
scope: Random scenes: height and width are each 8..30 by default, and the controls accept 4..30. Sides above 25 are a synthetic extension. Background is any colour except 1 and 6; colours 0, 2, 7 and 9 are a synthetic extension. There are 1..8 joined pairs (default 1..4) in both diagonal orientations. Segment lengths run from 2 steps (low probability) to min(h,w)-1. Each segment has 0..3 trigger 6s, which are sometimes consecutive and sometimes adjacent to an endpoint. Some scenes share an endpoint 1 between two perpendicular pairs, which is a synthetic extension. Segments may cross each other, and 6-lines may cross each other. Distractor lone 1s and lone 6s include these near misses: a 6 next to a segment, a 6 on a segment's extension beyond an endpoint, a 1 with a near-equal diagonal index, and a 1 in the same row or column as another 1. Deliberately not supported: a 6-line crossing a foreign segment interior or a pre-existing object, because the convention is undetermined. Also not supported: diagonally adjacent 1s with an empty segment, and explicit scenes with no pairs. Explicit latent scenes reconstruct all canonical fixtures.

authored_constraints: Background colour is not 1 or 6 and is the strict plurality colour of the input.
Explicit pairs list exactly the set of diagonal-sharing 1 pairs, with at least one pair.
No 1-cell lies strictly inside any segment.
Every 6 on a segment interior is a trigger. The perpendicular line of a trigger never passes over any other input object or any segment interior.
Random endpoints and triggers are not 8-adjacent to unrelated objects. The exceptions are a trigger next to its own endpoint and consecutive triggers on the same segment, both of which are allowed.
Lone 1s share no diagonal with any other 1. Lone 6s and lone 1s avoid segment interiors and 6-line cells.
Every joined pair changes at least one cell, so outputs are never identical to inputs.
All sampling uses bounded retries (300 scenes x 80 pair attempts x 140 distractor attempts); otherwise a ValueError is raised.
